reason: The contract (problem.txt) requires abs(actual[i] - atan(x[i])) <= 1e-6 for every finite FP16 value, as a single global verdict. Confirmed in-scope runtime evidence shows this is violated broadly: probe t9 (c1) scanned the full FP16 lattice in [0.5,2.5] both signs and found 1174/3866 middle-interval elements over tolerance, max error 5.03e-6 near the 0.66 seam (x=-0.6220703125); probe t10 (c2) found 1630/3672 upper-branch elements (|x|>2.414213562373095) over tolerance, max error 3.26e-6 at x=-2.416015625. These are ordinary, in-domain FP16 values, not edge cases; the failures are systematic (hundreds to thousands of lattice points), not single-point ties or negligible near-zero absolute differences — errors reach 3-5x the tolerance. c3 (extrema ±65504) was rebutted (error only ~5e-8), showing the defect is in the FP32 rational evaluation in the middle and upper intervals, not at the extremes. All open claims have evidence, and the Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and recorded no new claims. The declared contract permits approximations but only if they meet the 1e-6 absolute tolerance throughout the entire legal domain; the confirmed evidence shows they do not. Reject.
